u0: No client request is outstanding: any arrival so far has had its order taken, food handled, and service completed. This is the neutral between-orders stage, where the agent can wait for the next client. When a new client arrives, take their order, fetch and prepare food, and serve it.
u1: A client's order has been taken, but no food has been acquired yet and the order has not been served. The waiting order requires fetching a portion from the pantry, preparing it, and delivering it. Acquiring food advances the task to the serving phase; until then both the food and service requirements remain open.
u2: The service requirement from an earlier order has already been cleared, but the requirement that food be taken in hand for that order remains outstanding. Obtain a portion of food to settle the remaining food-handling requirement. No further serving is needed for that earlier order; a new arrival would begin a fresh order.
u3: A client's order has been taken and the food requirement has already been met at least once, but the order still awaits service. Prepare the food if it is raw and deliver it to the waiting client; if it has slipped from the agent's hands, recover or fetch another portion first. Service is the only remaining requirement for this order.
u4: A client has arrived and is waiting for their order to be taken; no earlier order requirements are outstanding. Take the order from the waiting client. Once it is taken, the task moves on to obtaining or preparing food and serving the client.
u5: An order-taking requirement from a newly arrived client coexists with an earlier taken order that still needs food and has not been served. Take the new client's order while also fetching and preparing food for the earlier order and eventually serving it. Neither order is finished until its order-taking, food, and service requirements are all cleared.
u6: A client is waiting to have their order taken, and an earlier order still has an outstanding food-handling requirement; that earlier order's service has already been handled. Take the new order and obtain food to clear the earlier food requirement. The earlier order no longer needs to be served again.
u7: A client has arrived and needs their order taken, while an earlier taken order remains unserved even though its food requirement was already met. Take the new order, then make sure prepared food is in hand and serve the earlier waiting client. If that food has slipped away, recover or replace it before serving; otherwise the earlier order only needs delivery.
